title: The Biggest Commodity Boom Since 1980 Is HERE… And It's Still EARLY
speaker: Ross Givens

macro_themes.view: The commodity boom is still early because supply takes ~17 years to respond while demand turns on quickly.
IEA projects a 25% copper mine-supply shortfall by 2035, which should keep pushing copper higher.
China's central bank and households keep buying gold (23 straight months), supporting dips.
A global recession is the main short-run risk to copper; a Chinese property/stock recovery could cool gold buying.

calls.reason: Grasberg recovery from ~67% to full capacity by end-2027 into a copper shortage, with gold by-product; monthly chart breaking out barely above its 2008 peak.
calls.quote: Freeport is about to be selling a lot more copper into a market that is short of it, and that is a pretty good place to be.

calls.reason: Down ~40% from highs on a small production miss while raising shareholder returns to 50% of FCF; operating leverage could drive 50-70% upside if gold recovers.
calls.quote: the same reason Kinross is down 40% right now is what could make it go 50, 60, 70% higher.

calls.reason: IEA sees a 25% mine-supply shortfall by 2035 and new mines take 17 years; shortage hasn't shown up yet.
calls.quote: the IEA is telling you the shortage hasn't even shown up yet.

calls.reason: Persistent Chinese central-bank and household buying; pullback from $5,500 high seen as a normal first pullback in a long boom.
calls.quote: A central bank that buys every month for 2 years isn't trading the chart. It's just buying every dip.

notes: FCX price_at_call 72 approximates 'trades in the low 70s'. Gold 4000 approximates 'just over $4,000'. Copper 6.64/lb is the stated current price at the end of a 10-year comparison.
